title: SLA Metric Binding and Credit Computation Guidelines for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Define an unambiguous, auditable measurement and crediting scheme for Dedicated capacity throughput commitments that covers: per-tenant throughput attainment, quantile-based windowing, autoscaling and failover exemptions, and a deterministic credit computation algorithm acceptable for contract language. This ticket consolidates engineering telemetry inputs, legal-friendly phrasing, and the credit math used to compute monetary or consumption credits when commitments are not met.
acceptance_criteria: A1: SLA metric definition that maps committed units (requests/minute or tokens/sec) to an evaluated time-series and an exact aggregation function.
A2: Error budget / credit computation formula with worked examples for common failure modes (peak shortfall, sustained degradation, AZ failover).
A3: Contract clause draft approved by Legal and Sales that can be copy-pasted into new customer offers.
A4: Instrumentation checklist and monitoring queries for the Console to show per-customer SLA attainment and remaining error budget.
A5: Autoscale and capacity-change exemption rules clearly documented and incorporated into the credit computation so credits are not given when customer-driven changes or scheduled maintenance occur.
A6: Implementation spike PR and dashboard prototype linked from this ticket.
A7: Regression test plan for synthetic load tests that reproduce credit calculations across representative traffic patterns.
notes: 2025-11-11: Kickoff sync with Engineering (Runtime + Infra), Legal, and Sales. Agreed to measure throughput on 1-minute windows and evaluate on rolling 24-hour quantiles. Action: Eng to validate 1-min granularity is available in current telemetry (Marco).

2025-11-13: Engineering update — runtime exposes per-tenant tokens_per_min and request_success_rate metrics; need small addition to annotate autoscale events and region failovers in metrics stream. Estimate: 3d. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842)

2025-11-14: Product/Legal alignment — Legal prefers credit expressed as percentage-of-monthly-commitment not absolute dollars to allow standardized SOW language. Sales requests a bounded maximum credit (<= 25% of monthly fee).
2025-11-15: Design note — Console should surface the rolling attainment heatmap and a time-series showing minutes below threshold so customers can verify credits. UX spike scheduled CYCLE-2025-W48.

2025-11-17: Decision: use a quantile-linked SLA: customer commitment is met if at least Q% of 1-minute windows over the billing window meet or exceed the committed throughput. Default quantile: 95th percentile (configurable per contract). Rationale: resilient to short spikes and aligns with observed runtime variability.

2025-11-18: Trade-offs discussed — higher quantiles (99%) are stricter but increase engineering cost; lower quantiles (90%) risk masking frequent short degradations. Defaulting to p95 provides balance for most enterprise customers.
Follow-ups: Legal to accept draft clause, Eng to implement metric annotation for autoscale/failover events, PM to prepare customer-facing FAQ and examples.
contract_language_draft:
Draft clause (for inclusion in Service Schedule): 

'Throughput Commitment. Provider shall make Available for Customer a sustained throughput level (the 'Committed Throughput'), measured in tokens per minute or requests per minute as specified in the Order Form. Provider measures Committed Throughput on 1-minute measurement windows. For each billing period, the Committed Throughput is considered met if at least the Xth percentile (the 'Throughput Quantile') of the 1-minute measurement windows within the billing period meet or exceed the Committed Throughput. The default Throughput Quantile is the 95th percentile unless otherwise specified.

Credits. If the Committed Throughput is not met for the billing period, Customer will receive a credit (the 'Throughput Credit') computed as set forth in the Throughput Credit Formula. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for breaches of the Throughput Commitment under this Schedule and are subject to the exclusions and limitations set forth herein, including scheduled maintenance, customer-initiated scale-downs, and catastrophic region failovers as defined in the Provider's operational playbooks. The aggregate credits for any single billing period shall not exceed twenty-five percent (25%) of the monthly recurring charge for the Dedicated capacity in that billing period.'
error_budget_formula:
Definitions: 
Committed = C (units/min), ObservedMinute[i] = O_i for minute i, BillingWindow = N minutes (typically calendar month).

Step 1 — Minute pass/fail: pass_i = 1 if O_i >= C else 0.
Step 2 — Throughput Quantile Attainment (TQA): TQA = 100 * (sum(pass_i) / N). (This is percent of minutes that meet or exceed C.)

If TQA >= QuantileThreshold (e.g., 95), then no credit. If TQA < QuantileThreshold then compute ShortfallFactor = 1 - (TQA / QuantileThreshold).

Throughput Credit (%) = min(MaxCreditPct, ShortfallFactor * ScalingFactor) where ScalingFactor converts percent shortfall into a billing credit (default ScalingFactor = 1.0) and MaxCreditPct = 25%.

Worked example: C=1200 req/min, QuantileThreshold=95, N=43200 (30-day month * 24*60). If only 41,580 minutes met C then TQA = 100*(41580/43200)=96.2 -> no credit. If 40,500 minutes met C then TQA = 93.75, ShortfallFactor = 1 - (93.75/95) = 0.01316 -> Credit% = 1.316% of monthly fee.
monitoring_queries: KQL: telemetry.events | where tenantId == '<customer>' and eventType == 'autoscale' | project timestamp, delta_instances
Alert: SLA-EVALUATION-ANOMALY -> when observed_minute_count_for_customer < expected_minute_count for 10m (investigate metric pipeline gaps)
implementation_plan: Step 1: Telemetry changes — annotate per-tenant metric stream with autoscale and failover markers (Eng runtime) — 3d
Step 2: Compute service — new microservice that evaluates minute-level pass/fail and stores daily aggregates for customers — 5d
Step 3: Console UX — heatmap + time series and credit estimator (Design + Frontend) — 6d
Step 4: Legal review and final contract text (Legal) — 2d
Step 5: Synthetic test harness and validation using replayed production traffic (SRE + Eng) — 4d
Step 6: Pilot with two existing Dedicated customers (Sales) — 2 billing cycles
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Metric cardinality and ingestion cost with 1-minute per-tenant resolution. Mitigation: roll-up older data and only retain minute-level for current 30 days; use sampling for low-volume tenants.

Risk: Credits awarded for provider-initiated autoscale cold-starts. Mitigation: mark autoscale cooldown windows (e.g., 5 minutes after scale event) as exempt from credit computation per agreed policy.
Risk: Disputes from customers about the measurement windows. Mitigation: provide interactive export of raw minute-level data and a deterministic calculation tool in the Console for transparency.
Risk: Legal pushback on uncapped credits. Mitigation: include MaxCreditPct cap (25%) and carve-outs for force majeure, scheduled maintenance, customer-induced changes.
